---
applyTo: "resources/views/**/*.blade.php"
---

# Blade View Guidelines

- Reuse the existing `layouts/`, `sections/`, `partials/`, `components/`, and `forms/` view patterns. Use `@extends`, `@section`, `@yield`, and `@include` consistently with neighboring templates.
- Follow Sage 10 and Acorn view conventions; use data supplied by view composers, controllers, or block render callbacks rather than querying for or assembling application data in templates.
- Keep templates focused on presentation. Do not add complex business logic; move data preparation and behavior to the existing PHP application or component layers.
- Escape dynamic text and attributes with Blade's escaped `{{ }}` output or the appropriate WordPress escaping function. Use raw `{!! !!}` output only for trusted or explicitly sanitized HTML, such as markup generated by WordPress or WooCommerce.
- Preserve semantic HTML and accessibility, including heading order, meaningful link and button labels, and existing ARIA attributes.
- Avoid changing established markup or CSS classes unless the requested behavior requires it; reuse existing classes and tokens.
- Do not add inline styles when existing CSS or Tailwind classes can express the presentation.
